sections.html:
Start with the state line, because Texarkana is two cities. A house on the Texas side sits in Bowie County and follows Texas law. One across State Line Avenue in Arkansas follows Arkansas rules and is recorded in Miller County. This page covers the Texas side.

If you are unsure which side you are on, check the county printed on your tax bill or deed. Bowie means Texas. That one detail decides which laws, which appraisal district and which clerk apply to everything that follows.

For a Texas address, a quick sale usually takes one of three shapes, and each suits a different seller.

  • Cash purchase: no mortgage to approve, so closing waits only on clean title.
  • Agent listing: a bigger audience, paired with inspections and lender deadlines.
  • Sale with repair terms: after inspection the buyer asks for fixes or a credit toward them.

The Texas city grew from a railroad junction founded on December 8, 1873, and it was chartered in 1876. The two halves keep separate mayors, councils and officials, yet share fire service, food and dairy inspection, sewage disposal and some recreation. The Federal Building straddles the line.

Interstate 30 meets four U.S. highways here, and the local economy rests on timber, farmland, minerals and rail. Texarkana College, three major hospitals and Wright Patman Lake round out the picture. Hospital and college staff, plus people commuting along I-30, are the natural buyers for a Texarkana listing.

A 2015 estimate put the Texas city at 37,280 people, within a metro area covering all of Bowie County and Miller County, Arkansas. Treat that as scale only. Your house competes across a small two-state market where employers on both sides pull workers toward either city. For a current pricing picture, a Bowie County title company or the appraisal district can help.

sections.h2: Selling points for a Texarkana house
sections.html:
Buyers respond to what the area offers day to day. Texarkana serves as a trading and industrial hub reaching into Oklahoma and Louisiana, with cotton, corn, rice, soybeans and pecans grown nearby and lumber, rail tank cars and paper products made here.

  • Education and medicine: Texarkana College, which includes a nursing department, and three major hospitals.
  • Recreation: Wright Patman Lake, Millwood Reservoir across the line, and the annual Four States Fair and Rodeo.
  • Transportation: Interstate 30 and four U.S. highways cross here, and the city is a major Southwest rail center.

Parts of town were built out by 1896, with waterworks, streetcars and brick schools, which hints that many houses here are old. If yours has decades behind it, expect buyers to ask when wiring, plumbing and the roof were last redone. Receipts and permits answer that quickly. Without them, an inspector will do the answering, and not always in your favor.

sections.h2: Tax calendar for a Texarkana seller
sections.html:
Bowie Central Appraisal District follows the statewide schedule from the Texas Comptroller.

Annual tax calendar
DateWhat happens
January 1Values set; tax lien attaches
April 30Many exemption applications due
May 15Usual protest deadline, or 30 days after the mailed notice, if later
October 1Bills mailed
January 31Final day before delinquency
February 1Delinquent; 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest begin

The Bowie CAD website links to a payment portal, a property tax calendar, an exemption breakdown and a page on proposed rates. Need a payoff figure for your own account? Use the portal or phone the Bowie County tax office.

sections.h2: How to protest a Bowie CAD appraisal
sections.html:
Your window closes May 15, or 30 days after the notice is sent if that comes later. Each spring Bowie CAD mails a notice to owners whose market value climbed by at least $1,000, with market, assessed and taxable figures side by side.

  • By mail: P.O. Box 6527, Texarkana, TX 75505.
  • In person: 122A Plaza West in Texarkana or 710 James Bowie Drive in New Boston.
  • Online: through the portal, using the owner ID and PIN printed on the notice.

Once you file, request an informal sit-down with an appraiser. Those start April 16 and each property gets one. Refuse the settlement offer and the appraisal review board takes the case. Somebody else can speak for you if you sign an appointment of agent form.

On a main residence, a homestead exemption lowers taxable value, and appraised value can rise no more than 10 percent a year. Someone buying to live in the house will ask what ownership costs after their own exemption kicks in.

State rules give school districts a $140,000 homestead exemption. Seniors and disabled owners receive extra relief and a school tax ceiling that can travel with them to a different Texas home. Disabled veteran exemptions scale by rating. File through Bowie CAD, and ask how to end your own exemption after you sell.

Delinquent taxes get paid from your proceeds. Because the lien follows the property, the title company will ask for a payoff figure. Homestead owners may find collectors willing to set up plans of up to 36 months.

Heirs of an inherited house can probate the will, request a muniment of title, or use a deed naming a beneficiary that was recorded while the owner lived. Foreclosure sales fall on the first Tuesday of a month after 21 days' notice. Against squatters, Property Code chapter 24B lets you ask the sheriff or constable to act, but not against family members or current or former tenants.

Texas lets a seller close with taxes owed, so a balance does not block a sale. It simply gets settled at the closing table. Your own facts matter, so see a Texas attorney. Before that visit, collect the deed, your latest tax statement, any loan statement and a list of everyone living in the house. Most of these situations are workable for a cash buyer as long as title can be cleared by the day you pick. Sellers who start the paperwork early usually have the most choices about timing.

After a Texas-side sale funds, the deed goes to the Bowie County Clerk, the office for the county where the land sits. Your title company handles that step in the normal course. Ahead of closing, request a written lender payoff that stays good through your closing date. Put every roof, plumbing and electrical receipt in one folder so a buyer sees the history at a glance. On closing day, bring photo ID, every key and any garage remotes, and arrange to stop utilities in your name that same day.

faqs.q: Is my Texarkana house governed by Texas or Arkansas law?
faqs.a: By the law of the state where it sits. A Texas-side house is in Bowie County and uses Texas rules. Your deed and tax bill show the county.

faqs.q: When must I protest my Bowie CAD value?
faqs.a: By May 15, or 30 days after the notice is mailed if that is later. Informal meetings come first, then the appraisal review board.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Texarkana house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. At closing, the balance plus any penalty and interest is paid from your proceeds. Request a payoff from the tax office that covers your closing date.

faqs.q: Do I have to repair a house before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No. Cash buyers often take a house as is, while a mortgage buyer is likelier to ask for repairs. Either way, collect receipts for major systems, since a clear paper trail speeds a decision.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed for a Texas-side sale?
faqs.a: At the Bowie County Clerk's office, in the county where the land lies. Your title company ordinarily files it for you.
